cases.description: SELF-APPROVAL CHECK: this campaign's M5 mission notes, verbatim as captured 2026-10-06, with no campaign notes. Its heading does not match, and its example record is indented, so M5's notes must not approve M5
cases.missionNotes:
## Plan review record shape (decision, final 2026-10-05)

Campaign decisions 9-12 settled the open questions. The rule is AC1; in short:
- Strict record. This is what the planner writes, and it prints no warning. The example below is indented so it is not itself a record:
    ## Plan review (Alex + Rio, 2026-10-05)
    Reviewers: ba (Alex), tech-lead (Rio)
    Verdict: approved with nits
- Legacy record, accepted with a set-status.js warning: a heading that names both reviewers by role token or by the persona names Alex and Rio, with no column-0 Reviewers: or Verdict: line in its section. The real example is solo uwb-ranging-ingest-vendor-v01's campaign notes.
- Never counts: `## Plan review overridden (...)`; a Reviewers: line that names only persona names; a Verdict other than approved or approved with nits; a Verdict line without a Reviewers line; a heading that names one reviewer; indented lines; lines after the next `## ` heading.
- Self-approval check (rule spike, 2026-10-05, scratchpad pr2-spike.mjs, run on these notes after this edit): this section's heading does not match `^## Plan review \(` and its examples are indented, so these M5 notes alone are refused. The campaign's own record is strict and is allowed with no warning.
- Gated: a move INTO executing from any other stored status (decision 11). A refusal exits 3, because exit 1 already means 'no entity' and exit 2 means usage. Override: `--force=<reason>` on the script, the modal confirm in the UI. Both append `## Plan review overridden (<YYYY-MM-DD UTC>)` plus the reason, so the bypass is on the board.
- One rule, two implementations: plan-review.mjs (pack, dependency-free, imported by set-status.js) and its mirror planReviewStatus in packages/board (used by BoardHost.setStatus). packages/board/test/plan-review-parity.test.ts holds them together over a shared table and every real notes pair. This is the dual-implementation hazard of entity-io.mjs and entity-schema.ts. The dropdown calls BoardHost.setStatus, never the script. The confirm is a host modal (DispatchCtx.dialog.confirm), not webview UI. The work-log and mission-gate hooks act only on a status change that happened (M2-AC8), so a refused start is never logged.
- Spike results on real data (2026-10-05): solo has 115 missions, and 6 are allowed (all uwb, legacy, through the campaign notes). This campaign has 6 of 6 allowed (strict, through the campaign notes).

## Planning notes (Rio, 2026-10-05)

User decisions 3 and 6 apply (UI enforcement; AGENTS.md § Test lanes; qa-env.mjs config-driven; mission-input.js retired in M2).
Solo's .agents/manual-qa/qa-db.sh hard-codes EDGESERVER_* and is the model for qa-env.mjs (exit 3 refused, exit 4 probe mismatch).
Octoshell's lanes: fast = `pnpm --filter <pkg> test`, coverage = `pnpm coverage`; parked-test baseline is one allowed skip: packages/graph/test/vault-calibration.test.ts:10 describe.skipIf(!HAS_VAULT).
Real plan-review examples: this campaign's own notes carry the strict record of 2026-10-05 (the allow case). Solo uwb-ranging-ingest-vendor-v01's campaign notes carry a heading-only record from 2026-10-02 (the legacy accept-with-warning case; its M5 is cancelled, and cancelled -> executing is a gated move). Solo epic-013 M10 ('M10 - One setup flow, preset warnings, and edge-side exception authorization') is draft, and neither it nor its campaign has a record (the refuse case).

cases.campaignNotes:
## User decisions (2026-10-05)

1. **Workflow support is removed from octoshell ENTIRELY**: pack, board library and extension. Old `workflows/` folders are ignored by the model; validate.js, validateBoard and doctor.js give a non-fatal warning. Files are never touched (no activation-time migration, no auto-delete). (Refined by 13(d): an agent running octobots-doctor may remove one folder after the user says yes to that folder.)
2. **Tests pairing is a WARNING ONLY.** validate warns when a mission has no linked tests/m<n>/ or has ACs not covered by test cases. It is never an error and never blocks `set-status.js ... done`.
3. **Plan review is ENFORCED in both the script and the UI.** set-status.js AND the extension's status dropdown (BoardHost.setStatus) refuse to move a mission to `active` until a BA + tech-lead plan-review sign-off is recorded (shape defined in M5 AC1). Override: `--force` on the script, a confirm dialog in the UI. (Refined by decisions 9-11 on 2026-10-05: a legacy heading-only record is accepted with a warning, reviewers are matched by role token, and only moves into `executing` are gated. The script override is `--force=<reason>` and a refusal exits 3.)
4. **Campaign-level branches get their own campaign-level cost row** in tokenomics, not split across missions. A branch containing the campaign slug without -m<n> (feat/<slug>, chore/<slug>-plan, campaign/<slug>) belongs to the campaign row; an explicit `branches:` declaration on the campaign also counts. ## Test conventions (every TC and QA task)

1. A TC that runs a vitest suite runs `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec vitest run <package-relative path> --reporter=verbose` and expects at least 1 test passed in that file; the owning task's AC names the file (repo-relative). `pnpm --filter <pkg> test -- <name>` is never used: the extension's `--passWithNoTests` exits 0 when no file matches.
2. Vitests that need real boards read `OCTOBOTS_BOARD_COPIES` (colon-separated `.octobots` directories). When it is unset (CI), they copy the repo's own `.octobots/` into a temp dir, so they still run real data and still pass at least one test. QA points it at `cp -R` copies of solo and octoshell.
3. QA harnesses are committed plain-node scripts under `apps/vscode-extension/scripts/qa/`, each owned by a task and smoke-tested by a vitest: tokenomics-report.mjs (T1.2), install-pack.mjs (T2.3), dump-ids.mjs (T3.3), dump-tests.mjs (T6.1). There is no `.qa/` directory.
4. Result words map to TC status: PASS -> pass, FAIL -> fail, BLOCKED -> blocked, UNREACHABLE -> blocked with the reason in the RUN file. A manual (F5) execution is noted as manual in the RUN file; its status is still pass, fail or blocked. (M4's TC format contract.)
5. Every tokenomics command passes `--project-dir`: agent shells reset the cwd between calls, and a bare rollup.mjs writes octoshell's own runs.json. Each collect run that is compared starts from an empty raw/segments.jsonl (collect.mjs merges into the existing file).
6. TC shell is portable (BSD/macOS): awk, not GNU sed extensions. The body of a TC without its frontmatter is `awk 'c>=2{print} /^---$/{c++}' <file>`.
7. set-status.js is `set-status.js <parent-dir> "<exact title>" <state>`; for a mission the parent is the campaign dir. doctor.js --json prints `{root, packVersion, findings:[{level, area, msg, fix}]}`. Once M5 lands, moving a mission into executing without a plan review needs `--force=<reason>` (accepted in any argv position), and a refusal exits 3.
8. Every task that changes packages/board (T1.3, T3.3, T4.2, T5.2, T6.1): after a root `pnpm build`, run `pnpm --filter @octoshell/vscode-extension graph:payload:write`, and if the bytes changed, rewrite the 57 hash in apps/vscode-extension/scripts/graph-payload-versions.json as a visible diff line in the same PR.
9. Every change to a pack SKILL.md (from M7 on): run `node apps/vscode-extension/scripts/shipped-skills.mjs --write` and commit the updated store in the same PR; the extension's build runs `--verify` and fails otherwise.
